question: What term describes the broad strategy used by an educator to deliver instruction?
explanation: A teaching method refers to the overall strategy and plan chosen to facilitate learning outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h1)

question: How does a teaching technique differ fundamentally from a teaching method?

options.A: A technique is a narrower procedure used within the broader method
options.B: Methods rely on digital tools whereas techniques are purely manual
options.C: A method is only used for clinical settings unlike techniques
options.D: Techniques focus strictly on testing rather than instructional delivery

explanation: Techniques represent the specific styles and steps executed inside the framework of a larger teaching method. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h1)

question: Which instructional approach relies primarily on the educator talking while learners listen passively?
explanation: The lecture method is a classic teacher-centred approach designed for delivering bulk information to large audiences. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of strictly teacher-centred methods in professional nursing training?

options.A: They take significantly longer to cover basic definitions than group work
options.B: They prevent educators from ever assessing student knowledge levels
options.C: They restrict active student participation and clinical reasoning practice
options.D: They require too many expensive digital gadgets to run effectively

explanation: Because communication flows mainly one way, learners have fewer chances to practice critical thinking and hands-on problem solving. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h2)

question: Why is problem-based learning particularly effective for training student nurses?

options.A: It connects theoretical knowledge directly to realistic clinical scenarios
options.B: It eliminates the need for any independent reading or library research
options.C: It focuses exclusively on memorizing normal laboratory reference ranges
options.D: It ensures all students finish their syllabus at the exact same hour

explanation: Problem-based learning uses realistic cases to prompt self-directed inquiry and practical clinical reasoning. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h3)

question: What small-group technique involves splitting a large classroom briefly to discuss a specific clinical question?
explanation: Buzz groups allow rapid, small-group interaction and idea generation right in the middle of a larger teaching session. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of using medical simulation in nursing education?

options.A: It removes all forms of stress associated with emergency healthcare
options.B: It guarantees that every student passes their board examinations easily
options.C: It permits safe practice of procedures without risking real patient safety
options.D: It completely replaces the need for clinical supervision in the wards

explanation: Simulation creates a controlled environment where learners can make mistakes and learn from them safely. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h4)

question: When is a post-clinical conference most effectively utilized by a nursing educator?

options.A: Before the semester begins to assign textbook reading chapters
options.B: Immediately after ward duties to review experiences and care plans
options.C: During a written examination to prevent students from cheating
options.D: Only at graduation to evaluate final cumulative grade points

explanation: Post-clinical conferences allow students to reflect on real patient encounters and consolidate their practical learning right away. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a Learning Management System in education?

options.A: To restrict student access to online nursing research textbooks
options.B: To host course materials, assignments, and track student academic progress
options.C: To replace clinical instructors during invasive surgical procedures
options.D: To automatically diagnose patient illnesses in hospital emergency rooms

explanation: An LMS serves as a centralized digital hub for distributing educational content and managing class interactions. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h5)

question: Why must educators exercise caution when introducing digital tools into the nursing curriculum?

options.A: Technology prevents any form of collaborative group work in class
options.B: Digital applications always cause students to forget basic anatomy facts
options.C: Computers cannot be used to teach psychomotor nursing skills
options.D: Tools must support clear learning goals rather than serving as empty novelties

explanation: Technology is only effective if it directly enhances understanding of the curriculum rather than distracting learners. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h5)

question: Why must a nurse educator consider the nature of the subject matter when picking a teaching method?

options.A: All nursing subjects can be taught effectively using identical slide presentations
options.B: Theoretical topics cannot be explained using digital multimedia tools
options.C: Practical psychomotor skills require hands-on demonstrations rather than lectures alone
options.D: Clinical postings are unnecessary if the syllabus is short enough

explanation: Different types of knowledge—cognitive, affective, and psychomotor—demand tailored instructional approaches for effective mastery. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h6)

question: Which factor relates directly to classroom size and student learning readiness?
explanation: Learner characteristics include background knowledge, group size, and learning styles that guide method selection. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h6)

question: What type of assessment is conducted during a course to provide ongoing feedback for instructional adjustments?
explanation: Formative assessments happen during instruction to monitor learning progress and guide immediate teaching adjustments. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h7)

question: Why is student feedback regarding teaching methods valuable for nurse educators?

options.A: It guarantees that every student will pass their final semester exams
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical supervisors to grade student performance
options.C: It highlights areas of instruction that need clarity and continuous improvement
options.D: It determines the exact financial budget allocated to the nursing school

explanation: Feedback from learners gives educators direct insight into how well instructional strategies worked in practice. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h7)
